newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia calls for speedy end to Afghan fighting.
newsitem.headline: Russia calls for speedy end to Afghan fighting.

text.p: Russia's Foreign Ministry called on Friday for a speedy end to fighting in Afghanistan and said the seizure of the capital Kabul by the Islamic Taleban militia had only worsened the situation there.
"Concern is growing in Russia about the rising scale and intensity of the armed hostility in Afghanistan," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
The statement said the seizure of Kabul by the Taleban militia had made things worse in Afghanistan and brought the country "to the brink of political, economic and humanitarian catastrophe".

The militia, which hanged former president Najibullah after capturing Kabul from government forces, has set up a ruling council in Kabul to run the country as an Islamic state. Najibullah was the last Moscow-backed ruler of Afghanistan.
The Russian foreign ministry said the international community should coordinate efforts to end the fighting, with the United Nations playing a key role.

"Russia calls on the United Nations to face up to the Afghan conflict and play an effective role as the main impartial mediator able to bring all sides in the conflict towards a compromise solution," it said.
Russia has had little contact with rival groups in Afghanistan since 10 years of Soviet military intervention ended in 1989.
Relations have been complicated by frequent clashes with Islamic rebels along the Tajik-Afghan border, which is patrolled by Russian troops.
The Taleban militia, who held seven Russian airmen captive for about a year in Kandahar in southwest Afghanistan, are no friends of Moscow. The crew escaped last month.
The airmen had been forced by the Taleban fighters to land their chartered Ilyushin Il-76 plane which was carrying ammunition for the Kabul government.
